newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 8.

text.p: PRAVO - The Czech Social Democratic Party will still push for the resignations of Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Minister of Labour and Social Affairs Jindrich Vodicka and Interior Minister Jan Ruml.
- Investicni a Postovni Banka will decide whether or not they will issue GDRs by the end of October according to the bank's press spokesman Jan Rezek.

- Motoinvest has purchased at least 10 percent of Creditanstalt CEIF from Komercni Banka, giving them 27.29 percent of the investment fund. In return, Motoinvest sold shares in Vodni Stavby Praha to Komercni Banka. Until last week the company held 12.16 percent of this company.

- Tatra expects to increase its lorry production to 3,000, approximately 1,000 more than in 1995 according to sales manager Jiri Benes. This is in large part due to increased exports, including 800 lorries to the United Arab Emirates.

- The trade deficit is currently reaching the level where it will have to be followed closely, though there are still no reasons to take steps against imports, according to Minister of Trade and Industry Vladimir Dlouhy.

- The manager of Poldi Ocel and Bohemia Art, Vladimir Stehlik, has announced that he transformed Poldi Ocel sro into Poldi Steel a.s.. Stehlik, whose Bohemia Art owns 52.8 percent of Poldi, transformed the company without the knowledge of the minority shareholders, according to sources.

- By the end of the year the number of health insurance companies should decrease from the current total of 14 to 10 through mergers according to the president of the Federation of Health Insurance Agencies, Vladimir Kothera. The four insurance companies in question were not mentioned.
- The Czech Agriculture and Food Inspection has started inspecting imported onions and other selected vegetables at the border rather than once they reach the market.
- Hybler Group obtained 68 percent of the shares of Moravolena Sumperk from the National Property Fund in a public tender.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Czech monetary institutions posted a gross profit of 3.3 billion crowns in the first half of 1996, approximately eight billion crowns in the same period of 1995. Of the total 57 monetary institutions operating in the Czech Republic, 17 are in the red.
- Many majority shareholders are willing to sell their controlling blocks to new strategic investors if they were interested, according to research.
- Prvni Brnenska Strojirna a.s. (PBS) has signed a contract with Skodaexport for the exclusive representation of PBS products in southeast Asia.
